sentences.text: The type specimen is a nearly complete, well-preserved skeleton found alongside rhynchosaurs and cynodonts.
Gnathovorax had three teeth in its premaxilla, whereas Herrerasaurus had four.
Its teeth were thin, curved, and blade-like, with serrations on the rear and front edges of the upper teeth.
This animal is the only herrerasaurid with a scapula that curves backward, has an expanded tip, and is not fused to the coracoid.
The ischium possessed a hole at its base called an obturator foramen, a feature shared with lagerpetids but not other herrerasaurids.
Gnathovorax was a small predator reaching about 3 meters in length.
Lesions on the skull suggest the animal engaged in intraspecific combat involving face biting or claw raking.
Gnathovorax fossils were found in the Santa Maria Formation in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.
The only known species, Gnathovorax cabreirai, was described by Pacheco and colleagues in 2019.
The holotype specimen was discovered in 2014 at the Marchezan site in São João do Polêsine, Brazil.
A 2022 CT scan revealed that Gnathovorax lacked an invasive air sac system and had non-pneumatized bones.
Researchers reconstructed a digital endocast of the brain from the well-preserved holotype skeleton.
The brain contained a large floccular fossa lobe, which is generally associated with motor control of the eyes, head, and neck.
Most paleontologists interpret the large floccular fossa lobe as evidence of an active predatory lifestyle.
Gnathovorax likely possessed a sliding jaw articulation similar to other herrerasaurids, though preservation is insufficient to confirm this completely.
Striations are present on the distal edge of all teeth, and maxillary teeth also have striations on the mesial edge.
The skeleton was fossilized in a layer of mud alongside small articulated skeletons of prozostrodont cynodonts.
These fossil remains indicate a diverse animal community at the Marchezan site.
Evidence from the soft tissues aligns with other signs of meat-eating in herrerasaurids, such as tooth and claw structure.
Cladistic analysis places Gnathovorax in a polytomy with Herrerasaurus and Sanjuansaurus within the family Herrerasauridae.
Gnathovorax is classified within the order Saurischia.
Gnathovorax belongs to the family Herrerasauridae.
Cladistic analysis suggests Herrerasauridae, including Gnathovorax, are basal Saurischians outside of Theropoda and Sauropodomorpha.
Gnathovorax lived during the Carnian stage of the Late Triassic.
Gnathovorax lived during the Carnian stage of the early Late Triassic, approximately 233 million years ago.
Gnathovorax lived in what is now South America.
